frameworks.name: Avatar Clarity Decision Framework
frameworks.definition: When choosing between multiple customer avatars, evaluate which requires the least change to your day-to-day operations and delivery model; operational burden, not customer size alone, determines viability.

frameworks.name: Sales Motion ROI Calculation
frameworks.definition: Estimate close-rate improvement (e.g., 2% to 5% or 10%), multiply by expected volume and average deal size to quantify sales-system impact before investment.

claims.text: A wildfire sprinklers company (2.2M revenue in year one) with 2% paid and referral close rate (45-60% on referral), operating in both B2C and B2B channels, has no sales motion rather than a delivery constraint. At 50k average deal size, moving from 2% to 5% close rate on 8,000 insurance-mandated leads would generate approximately 15 million incremental revenue.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: High-net-worth and commercial avatars with proven demand

numbers.axis: close rate and revenue impact from sales system installation

anchors.region: current state (2% close rate, 8,000 closed leads at 50k avg deal)
anchors.value: 400M annual revenue potential, assumes no sales motion constraint

anchors.region: with 5% close rate (modest sales motion improvement)
with 10-20% close rate (full sales motion implementation)

bounded_by: Assumes insurance mandate converts to actual lead volume
Assumes delivery model scales without fundamental redesign
Assumes sales talent availability and training feasibility

claims.text: When evaluating whether to pursue a new customer avatar or market opportunity, the primary lens is: does this require me to materially change my day-to-day activities and delivery operations? If the day-to-day stays roughly the same, the decision tilts toward 'yes' regardless of whether the new market is larger or smaller.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Service-based business with delivery bottleneck risk
Multiple viable customer avatars with different scale profiles
claims.mechanism: Operational burden is the true constraint, not customer count. Preserving existing day-to-day operations allows founder leverage to scale without hiring or process redesign.
bounded_by: Does not apply to pure software or high-automation businesses
Does not apply when the smaller avatar requires different product

claims.text: Referral channels (45-60% close rate) dramatically outperform paid and cold outreach (2% close rate) in home services, indicating the business is market-limited (no sales motion) rather than product-limited.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Warm, referred leads arrive with high pre-qualification and trust; cold leads have no context of product value. The 23x gap (2% vs 45-60%) signals a missing sales motion for cold/paid channels, not product-market fit issues.
bounded_by: Assumes paid traffic and referral pools have equivalent buyer avatars
Does not control for self-selection bias in referral traffic

claims.text: Insurance mandate-driven lead generation (e.g., wildfire product mandate requiring insurance eligibility) creates a forced-adoption scenario where the buyer has intrinsic motivation to close, raising close probability significantly above discretionary-purchase channels.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Product mandated by insurance or regulatory requirement
Buyer perceives product as necessary to get insurance or comply with mandate
claims.mechanism: Regulatory or insurance-driven necessity eliminates buyer skepticism and objection handling burden. The buyer self-qualifies through the mandate itself.
bounded_by: Does not apply to discretionary consumer products
Does not apply if mandate is not actively enforced or monitored

claims.text: An upmarket pivot (from selling to the whole market to targeting high-net-worth private clients and commercial clients only) can improve close rate 4x in three months without changing the underlying product, indicating the issue was avatar clarity, not product-market fit.
claims.speaker: wildfire sprinklers company founder
conditions: Service business with broad initial positioning
Upmarket pivot to high-net-worth and commercial avatars
claims.mechanism: Narrower avatar removes buyer-diversity objection handling and sales qualification friction. Higher-net-worth buyers have faster decision cycles and higher urgency.

numbers.axis: close rate improvement from avatar clarity

anchors.region: upmarket pivot to high-net-worth and commercial (3 months post-pivot)

bounded_by: Three-month window is recent data; sustainability unclear
Does not control for seasonal or market factors in the comparison

examples.text: A wildfire sprinklers company at 2.2M revenue is on the verge of signing an insurance deal that will mandate their product to 16,000 of the insurer's clients. Unlike a guaranteed contract, these 16,000 leads must still be closed through individual sales outreach—the mandate creates lead generation (awareness and delivery obligation) but not automatic conversion.

In the wildfire protection space, the same product and market can operate at vastly different close rates: 2% on paid and cold channels, 45-60% on referral. This disparity persists within the same business (same product, same delivery, same installation process), ruling out delivery or product quality as the constraint.

practices.text: When facing a business decision, assess the operational burden on your day-to-day work before assessing the opportunity size. A smaller opportunity that requires no operational change is often higher-ROI than a larger one that requires restructuring.
Install a sales motion (systematized close process, objection handling, qualification framework) before scaling paid-traffic channels or relying on lead-volume multiplication.
Use close-rate disparity between channels (referral vs. cold) as diagnostic evidence of a missing sales motion rather than a product problem.
